title: Jahangir State And Religion In The First Half Of The 17th Century
definition: The reign of Jahangir (1605–1627) represents a period of continuity in the Mughal policy of 'Sulh-i-kul' (universal peace) while witnessing the emergence of orthodox pressures and the institutionalization of state-religion relations.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the evolution of Mughal secularism, the role of the Ulema, and the socio-political tensions that culminated in the reign of Aurangzeb.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Jahangir State And Religion In The First Half Of The 17th Century.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
